Context: serializer emits v2 while open reads removed v1 fields, causing 34 native failures; old parameter documents conflict. Target: one six-field v2 shape and one serializer/deserializer round-trip all payloads with strict failure semantics. Design Considerations: non-semantic delivery id, directional rotating mailbox token, encrypted typed header, authenticated bounded ciphertext and wire-byte goldens. Design Value: eliminates the central protocol split that invalidates all higher evidence. Constraints & Risks: remove v1 fields, registry, fixtures and compatibility parsers in the same migration; do not infer production readiness from unit round-trip alone.

acceptance_criteria.text: Every protected payload class round-trips through one canonical v2 wire format and malformed, tampered, stale, duplicate, expired or wrong-recipient input fails closed.
Source, tests, FFI, docs and gates contain no retired envelope fields or v1 internal registry.

commit.message: fix(secure-mesh): complete relay envelope v2 migration
commit.target: relay envelope serializer, parser, registry, FFI and fixtures

goal: Close identity, verify-before-send, pairwise ratchet, replay and lifecycle semantics in the shared Rust core.
description: Scope: identity/trust records, pairing, prekeys, Double Ratchet state, replay/skipped-key ledgers, file and lifecycle operations. Context: the envelope break invalidates existing protocol completion claims and current KT evidence is missing. Target: locally authorized trust gates send; restart-safe monotonic state and bounded ledgers protect command, result, file, TTL, delete, resend and acknowledgement flows. Design Considerations: Signal-style ratchet owner in Rust, atomic persistence, one-time prekeys and AAD-bound typed identity. Design Value: keeps cryptographic state consistent across clients and restarts. Constraints & Risks: no clock or plaintext fallback; external directory authority is completed in the next branch.

acceptance_criteria.text: Identity, trust change, revoke, one-time prekey, restart, rollback, replay, skipped-key bounds and lifecycle vectors pass through the shared owner.
Unverified, changed or revoked peers cannot send or receive protected work through UI, native or relay entry paths.

goal: Make external Key Transparency and MLS product readiness real rather than projected.
description: Scope: typed directory authority, persisted checkpoints, gossip/witness, OpenMLS authentication service, product wiring, FFI and readiness evidence. Context: production uses missing evidence and MLS readiness is hard-coded false; prior completed claim conflicts with current source. Target: pinned external log evidence authorizes identity and MLS membership; OpenMLS owns RFC 9420 mechanics and product policy emits current transitions. Design Considerations: RFC 9162 inclusion/consistency, atomic checkpoints, typed AuthorizedDirectoryLeaf and one-time KeyPackage. Design Value: removes self-derived trust and turns group readiness into auditable state. Constraints & Risks: client cannot own the production log signing key; unavailable server evidence blocks the broad claim.

acceptance_criteria.text: Pinned external signatures, inclusion/non-inclusion, consistency, checkpoint persistence and equivocation cases produce typed directory authorization.
MLS invitation, credentials, commit authorization, one-time KeyPackage, removal, epoch secrecy and FFI transitions drive readiness without constants.
